title: Wait for GitHub's rate limits instead of failing
description:
Measured on 2026-10-27: a full first fetch of posit-dev/great-tables (962 issues and pull requests, 1,707 comments) costs 50 GraphQL points and 18 REST requests, so even rstudio/rstudio's history takes about 1,000 of the 5,000 GraphQL points an hour. But adding many large repositories at once can still use up an hour's quota, and then:

- **A refused request failed its target**, which stored nothing and started over the next night. Now every GitHub request (REST, GraphQL, search, traffic) that's refused for a rate limit waits until the limit resets, from `Retry-After` (secondary limits) or `X-RateLimit-Reset` (primary limits), at most 65 minutes, and tries again, up to three times. GraphQL reports a used-up limit with HTTP 200 and a `RATE_LIMITED` error, which counts too. The search API's own retry from #9 is replaced by this.
- **The search budget** goes from 270 to 1,500 searches a night. devrel-io's 465 repositories already used 266, so every repository added had its monthly reconciliation skipped; the search API has no daily limit, so the budget only bounds the time (up to an hour at 25 a minute, enough for about 2,600 repositories a week).

title: Make the PyPI smoke test see a new release
description:
The PyPI smoke test failed for v1.2.0 and v1.3.0, and passed when re-run. PyPI serves its index pages with `cache-control: max-age=600`, and uv honours it: when the first install attempt came before the new version was on the index, uv cached that page, and the other 29 attempts, over 5 minutes, read the same page. A re-run on a fresh runner, with an empty cache, installed on the first attempt.

Each attempt now runs `uv tool install --refresh`, which ignores uv's cache, and no longer hides uv's error output, so a failure says why.

title: Keep reconciliation's searches within GitHub's rate limit
description:
The first gate run on devrel-io (posit-dev/devrel-io#6) opened its tracking issue with 67 `reconcile.unavailable` findings, all "API rate limit exceeded" at the same second. GitHub's search API allows 30 searches a minute, and velocirepo searched at exactly that pace, so a minute that reset slightly late refused a search; that one error then made every repository of the night unavailable.

- Searches are paced at 25 a minute instead of 30, so a night's 270 searches take about 11 minutes instead of 9
- A search that GitHub refuses for a rate limit (403 or 429 mentioning "rate limit") waits 65 seconds and tries again, twice at most
- When the searches stop early anyway, the totals that came back are still compared; only the repositories without any are unavailable

title: Use actions that run on Node 24
description: install-ci's workflow templates check out with `actions/checkout@v6` instead of `@v4`, and the action saves pending archives with `actions/upload-artifact@v6` instead of `@v4`. GitHub has deprecated Node 20, which both `@v4` versions run on. upload-artifact v5 to v7 change nothing else that the action uses: artifacts are still zipped by default, so the gate reads them as before.

title: Export a standalone DuckDB database with a data dictionary
description:
Implements docs/design/2026-10-data-dict.md, to be released as v1.2.0: velocirepo writes everything a [commons](https://github.com/posit-dev/commons) agent needs, so anyone who uses velocirepo can run one on their own data.

- `velocirepo export <dir> --data-dict` writes `velocirepo.duckdb`, a standalone database (plain tables, no views, no JSON-typed columns), and `data-dict.yaml`, a [data-dict](https://data-dict.tidyverse.org) dictionary of exactly that data
- The dictionary comes from the schema, the source metadata (every source now declares what a target is, its metrics, event and content types and the extra keys that become columns), the data (examples, ranges, coverage) and the new `[data_dict]` section of `velocirepo.toml`: notes, shared targets, enum values, definitions and glossary terms
- Every export format gets the same tables, now with `targets` (also in `build-db` and the live views), `metrics_filled` and `meta`, and `page`, `video_id`, `post_id`, `ref`, `author` and `state` as columns
- `--source` exports every table, filtered to the source; project fields the config leaves out are NULL; `content.tags` is a list
- CI installs the data-dict CLI so the tests validate the generated dictionary
- A user guide page, `user_guide/data-dict.qmd`, and the plan for devrel-agent's nightly deploy, `docs/design/2026-10-devrel-agent-deploy.md`

title: Detect and recover from data problems
description:
Implements the reliability design and plan (docs/design/2026-10-reliability*.md), released together as v1.1.0.

- Each day is fetched once it has ended in its source's time zone, with per-target watermarks
- `velocirepo check`: failed jobs, deprecations, integrity, volume, freshness, diff checks against HEAD or between commits, and reconciliation with GitHub's, CRAN's and Plausible's own totals
- Raw response archive as release assets, `replay`, `upload-archive` and `download-archive`
- `velocirepo gate`: the nightly run that only adds data, reporting by default and enforcing with `[settings] gate = "enforce"`, with held-back data, release, discard and repair runs, and a tracking issue
- `check-heartbeat`, `digest`, optional Healthchecks pings, and changelog monitoring
- Concatenation on or after the 8th, and writes into existing period files
- Live API tests, an incident suite with mutation tests, and a user guide chapter

Existing workflows keep working: the action's mode defaults to fetch. Regenerate them with `install-ci` to get the gate. The deviations from the plan are listed at the end of the plan.

title: Fix Plausible pagination, GitHub stars and the comments page limit
description:
Fixes found while repairing devrel-io's data after the October correctness review (#4).

## Plausible pagination

Plausible doesn't guarantee an order across pages without `order_by`. A backfill of opensource.posit.co for 2026-06-22 to 2026-10-16 (53,826 rows, 6 pages) returned 280 rows twice and missed 280 others. Breakdowns are now sorted by every dimension. Nightly runs fit on one page and weren't affected.

## GitHub stars

Since July 2026, GitHub only lists the stargazers of repositories the token can administer or collaborate on. For every other repository the list is empty, which the fetch treated as a quiet day, so stars silently stopped being recorded. In September GitHub added [`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/stargazers/history`](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-04-new-api-endpoint-provides-privacy-safe-star-history-data/), which returns stars per day for any repository, without users.

- `daily_stars` is now a record from that endpoint. Star events are no longer fetched.
- Each fetch re-reads the last 7 days: GitHub's days end in US Pacific time, and removed stars lower their day's count.
- Repositories without `daily_stars` get their whole star history once, so upgrading doesn't need a full re-fetch.
- `total_stars` records the current star count, and the `stars` badge uses it.
- The `metrics` view no longer turns star events into `daily_stars`, which would count stars twice. Existing star events stay in the `events` view.

For ggplot2 the history matches the stored star events within a few stars per year; by day, 94% of days match once the events are shifted to UTC−7.

## GitHub comments page limit

GitHub serves at most 300 pages of 100 of a repository's issue comments. A full re-fetch of positron, quarto or rstudio hit that limit, failed, and stored nothing (in devrel-io that wiped their history on 2026-07-28). Comments are now listed by last update and continue from the last update time seen. Comments created before the window and edited in it no longer end the listing early, since they can come anywhere in that order.

## Daily files are merged, not replaced

Writing records for a day replaced its daily file with just the new records. The star history writes `daily_stars` for past days whose other metrics it doesn't fetch, so in devrel-io a star history backfill dropped 44,619 `total_reactions` records from October's daily files, and the 7-day reread would have done the same every night. Stored records now stay unless the batch has a record of the same series for that day, like compaction already does for monthly and yearly files.

## Verification

- `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt` are clean. Each change comes with a test that fails without it.
- With this branch, positron (since 2022) and quarto (since 2020) were re-fetched in devrel-io. PRs and issues opened, merged and closed per year match GitHub's search counts, and summed `daily_stars` match the star counts.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Fix compaction data loss and the October correctness review findings
description:
Fixes the findings of the October correctness review. The review, the fix plan and a resolution table mapping each finding to its commits are in `docs/review/`.

## Compaction and resuming

- Late data (backfills, re-fetches, a crash during cleanup) is merged into existing monthly and yearly files instead of replacing them. Newer values win.
- A month or year is compacted only once its last day is stored. Before, a day missing at compaction time was never fetched: in production that cost CRAN the last day of every month (2026-07-31, 08-31 and 09-30).
- Compaction reports its errors, leftover temp files are never read as data, and re-fetching a day no longer drops `total_*` change points.

## Sources

- GitHub issues and PRs are listed by last update, so closes, merges, state and reactions of items opened before the fetch window are recorded. Before, `daily_issues_closed` and `daily_prs_merged` only counted same-day closes.
- Plausible is fetched through the day before yesterday, so its days are complete in every time zone.
- Other fixes: Homebrew dating, LinkedIn errors and paging, RSS 1.0 feeds, YouTube durations, GitHub comment paging and partial GraphQL errors.

## Commands and tooling

- `fetch` exits non-zero when any job fails, after storing what succeeded. Warnings are shown by default.
- `validate-data --fix` no longer destroys event or content files, and it now detects and repairs overlapping period files and leftover temp files.
- Badges use the current metric names, `export --project` includes content, rename rewrites the fetch log, and config and database writes are atomic.
- The installers verify checksums. `.env` quoting round-trips. MCP caps query limits and keeps exports inside the project.
- CI checks gofmt, `go vet` and the race detector.

## Upgrade notes

- **Existing workflows:** add `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` to the "Commit and push" step. Without it, a day on which any source fails commits nothing. `install-ci` and the installation guide include it.
- **Plausible:** data arrives one day later than before.
- **Badges:** `downloads` is the all-time sum of `daily_downloads` (PyPI, CRAN), and `pageviews` the sum of `daily_site_pageviews`.
- **Repair after upgrading:** see the runbook in `docs/review/2026-10-fix-plan.md`. Re-fetch the missing CRAN days, run `fetch-github --start-date <first tracked date>` once, and re-fetch Plausible history.

## Testing

- 106 new tests (292 → 398), including a randomized compaction property test and a 13-month cron simulation through the orchestrator.
- 49 of 49 injected bugs are caught by the suite, against 18 of 28 before.
- Verified end to end against the cranlogs API.

title: Break docs into multi-page user guide
description:

title: Wait for GraphQL and Plausible rate limits, and show running jobs
description:
Three problems that came up while backfilling 578 new repositories for posit-dev/devrel-io#14.

## GraphQL rate limit

#11 waits for GitHub's rate limits, but only recognizes GraphQL's `RATE_LIMITED` error. The requests made after the limit is used up get a different body, which v1.4.0 treats as an ordinary error, so the target fails instead of waiting:

```json
{"errors":[{"type":"RATE_LIMIT","code":"graphql_rate_limit","message":"API rate limit already exceeded for user ID …"}]}
```

That response comes with HTTP 200, `X-Ratelimit-Remaining: 0` and `X-Ratelimit-Reset`, taken from the archive of the failed run. `RATE_LIMIT` and the `graphql_rate_limit` code now count as a rate limit too, and the GraphQL test covers both bodies. Without the fix, the new case fails.

## Plausible's burst limit

Concurrent fetches of many sites hit Plausible's burst limit: `429 {"error":"Too many API requests in a short period of time. The limit is 60 per 10 seconds. …"}`. A refused query now waits and is tried again, up to 5 times. It waits as long as `Retry-After` says, or one more 10-second window each time if there's no `Retry-After`.

## Progress during long fetches

A job's line is printed only when the whole job is done. During a backfill, all four workers can spend many minutes on large repositories, so nothing is printed for a long time. The concatenation at the end is silent too, and can take minutes after a backfill. Now:

- every 30 seconds, a line lists the jobs that are still running, longest first: ` [812/1654] … running: sparklyr/github 12m3s, readxl/github 1m30s`
- the concatenation is announced when it starts, and with its duration when it's done.

This uses two new hooks on `fetch.Options` (`OnRunning`, `OnConcatenate`), which `fetch` and the `fetch-<source>` commands set. The gate doesn't set them, so its output stays the same.

`go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` pass.

title: Retry resolving the latest release, and ask the API when it fails
description:
posit-dev/devrel-io's nightly run of 2026-11-08 failed in the install step with `Could not resolve a valid velocirepo version`. The step follows `github.com/posit-dev/velocirepo/releases/latest` without `-f` or retries. When GitHub answers with an error page instead of the redirect, the last path segment is `latest`, which isn't a version, so the night was lost. A few minutes later the redirect worked again.

- The redirect is followed with `curl -f` and 5 retries.
- If it still names no version, the step asks `/repos/posit-dev/velocirepo/releases/latest` with the workflow's token, and logs a warning.
- The binary and `SHA256SUMS` downloads are retried too.

I tested both paths locally: the redirect, and the API fallback with the redirect forced to fail. Both resolve v1.4.0.
